smell_validity.evidence: The session record absorbs three unrelated subsystems' working state — raw cipher key words including fixup sets that persist after close, six delete-walk scratch fields, one shared name buffer — while dissolving cohesive records; every helper reads the single handle and session close finalizes all of it. Per-pass reserve/release buys no reuse, so the boundary from owner-scoped design is unmistakable.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Removing the hoist restores real boundaries: cipher, delete-walk and naming stop changing one shared record; session close stops finalizing three subsystems; the entry.name-to-scratch alias and fixup keys persisting past close are genuine traps. Gain is lasting ownership clarity within one layer — strong, but working-state placement, not an architecture-level restoration.

development_plausibility.evidence: Native style: CLEANUP, feature guards and zip_entry_enc_* naming match the file, and flattening keys so helpers avoid new parameters reads as believable convenience work. But the identical recipe repeating across all three areas, plus ideology-only moves — persisting close-time locals, reserving then releasing per pass — leave faint task-shaped regularity that ordinary evolution would not show.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: It names all four hoisted state groups, every lifecycle path (plain/password over file and streams, close rewrite, delete flavors) and exclusions (miniz.h, error strings, no new symbols). Byte-identical protected output blocks cipher redesign, the four-area checklist blocks partial cleanup, ownership clauses block drift — material risk reduction while still permitting records or per-call scope.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Four extraction areas each need a different code-supported decision: live keys persist across open→write→close and must satisfy the tdefl callback context; fixup sets are per-call in strict orig-decrypt/fix-encrypt order; the workspace is per-pass with restored error-path frees; names are per-call copies freed at entry-lifecycle exits. No one decision covers all.

localization_burden.evidence: Deciding whether a site needs repair combines indirect mechanisms: DEFLATE-selected tdefl registration dispatching per chunk into session cipher fields, plus entry.name aliasing the scratch with guard-dependent release in two close paths. Plausible-looking exclusions exist: the pre-existing enc_header_ofs sits among injected enc_* fields; zip->entry.state and comp are legitimate session nodes.

repair_coordination.evidence: Relocating creation flips both reuse and release timing across stages: workspace cleanup moves from caller release to each exit path, name frees move to lifecycle exits and both close paths together. Concrete partial failure: revert open-path seeding locally while write/close still read session keys — plain flows pass, protected bytes corrupt across the open→write→close chain.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: Best single rule — reintroducing one owner-record family for the cipher groups, or restoring per-pass workspace locally — covers roughly one cluster, about a third of touch sites. Record-wrapping leaves workspace and name scratch session-resident; per-call locals break live-key persistence and the callback context. No uniform rule examined reaches 40% coverage.

behavioral_risk.evidence: A wrong-lifetime edit passes ordinary calls and fails in special state: unseeded or stale key sets garble protected output, surfaced only by byte comparison; restoring per-call copies can leak on error exits that ctest never observes. Multiple silent paths are plausible, but no supplied test or execution records prove one unchecked, so score 4 is not established.
